definitions.explanation: A duration of 100 years. Used both literally for measured time and figuratively for 'a very long time' in set expressions.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}は{創業|そうぎょう}{百年|ひゃくねん}だ。
examples.english: This shop has been in business for one hundred years.

examples.japanese: {百年|ひゃくねん}に{一度|いちど}の{大雨|おおあめ}が{降|ふ}った。
examples.english: Rain that only falls once in a century fell.

examples.japanese: {百年|ひゃくねん}{前|まえ}には{想像|そうぞう}もできなかった{技術|ぎじゅつ}が{今|いま}は{当|あ}たり{前|まえ}になっている。
examples.english: Technology that was unimaginable a hundred years ago is now taken for granted.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {百年|ひゃくねん}{前|まえ}: a hundred years ago
- {百年|ひゃくねん}{後|ご}: a hundred years from now
- {百年|ひゃくねん}に{一度|いちど}: once in a century
- {創業|そうぎょう}{百年|ひゃくねん}: founded a hundred years ago

IDIOMS:
- {百年|ひゃくねん}の{恋|こい}も{冷|さ}める: even a hundred-year love cools — used when one moment destroys a long-built feeling
- {百年|ひゃくねん}{早|はや}い: a hundred years too early — dismissive: 'you're nowhere near ready'
